parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation, no facility or custody restrictions, no border or document rules affecting trans visitors are documented — the worst features are absent entirely, not merely mitigated. Law offers real protections: hate-speech crime covering gender identity (fine raised 2024), hate-crime sentencing aggravation, conversion-practices ban, and a self-ID recognition bill pending (resident-facing, climate signal only). Enforcement of hate-crime protection is inconsistent: two 2019 capital incidents drew no police action and clerical incitement sometimes unaddressed — a documented gap in recourse, not state hostility. Rule of law generally functions in a rights-coalition member implementing regional equality directives; no targeting of trans people by police is recorded. Unknowns (custody placement, nonbinary marker handling) are open questions, lightest weight. Thin formal machinery plus weak enforcement hold it below the 0.85 tier; overall profile sits in the reduced-risk band near the stronger end of 0.65–0.75.
